findings.issue: The `distributions` slot is not present in the supplied schema digest for the Dataset/CoreDataset class, and no such slot is listed among the 98 slots. Ten objects with keys `path`, `format`, `media_type`, `compression`, `md5`, `notes`, `conforms_to_standard` were emitted. If CoreDataset does not declare `distributions`, this block will fail validation; if it does declare it, `md5` and `path` are not keys attested by the digest for any listed range class. The bundle supports the file names and MD5 checksums, so the content is evidenced, but the container slot is unverified against the digest.

`compression` is emitted inside each distribution object. The digest defines `compression` as a top-level Dataset slot with a CompressionEnum range; it is not attested as a key on any distribution-like object. Shape unverified.

FileCollection required key is `id` and it also accepts the top-level slot listing, so `name` and `description` are admissible. However `urn:cm4ai:filecollection:if-images` declares `file_count: 3` with no `path`, while the sibling collections mixing `path` (single archive) and `file_count` (count of archives) use `file_count` inconsistently — for `perturbseq-atlas` and `release-metadata` a `file_count` of 1 with a `path` naming one zip, versus `if-images` with `file_count: 3` and no path. The unit of `file_count` is ambiguous across entries (number of archives vs. number of files within).

`total_file_count: 10` is set at the dataset level and matches the ten files listed in the June 2026 Dataverse record. But the `file_collections` entries sum to 3+2+2+1+1+1 = 10 only if each `file_count` counts archives, which conflicts with the slot description that `total_file_count` aggregates `file_collections[].file_count` as a count of files. The value is bundle-supported; the aggregation semantics are internally strained.

`counts: 53788` is attached to the immunofluorescence Instance. The bundle attributes 53,788 immunofluorescent images to the CM4AI portal as a project-wide figure, not to the June 2026 release that this record's `id` and `doi` designate. A `source_caveats` on the object discloses this, but the numeric value still populates a per-release record with an out-of-scope count.

`B2AI_SUBSTRATE:64` (Perturb-seq Data) is used for the CRISPRi perturbation instance — defensible. However `instances[1].data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:59` (Size Exclusion Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Data) and `instances[2].data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:58` (Mass Spectrometry Data) are correct, while `instances[0].data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:56` (Immunofluorescence Image) is correct. No defect in the enum values themselves; flagged only to record that all four resolve to defined B2AI_SUBSTRATE terms.

`B2AI_TOPIC:26` (Protein) is assigned to the AP-MS bait-prey interaction instance while `instances[1].data_topic` uses `B2AI_TOPIC:28` (Proteome) for SEC-MS. Both are AP/SEC mass-spectrometry protein-interaction readouts; the split between Protein and Proteome is an editorial distinction the bundle does not draw.

The bundle's Dataverse author list names approximately 46 contributors with ORCIDs and affiliations. Sixteen are emitted. The omission is disclosed in `source_caveats`, but the slot is multivalued and the bundle supports one Creator object per named contributor; selecting a subset without a stated selection rule that the bundle itself provides is an editorial reduction of clearly-supported evidence.

The Sali entry carries `source_caveats` describing an affiliation conflict, and simultaneously resolves the conflict by emitting only the UCSF affiliation. Recording only one side of a disclosed conflict inside a multivalued `affiliations` list, when the bundle supplies both, under-represents the evidence; both Organization objects could be listed.

Creator `id` values are minted as `urn:cm4ai:creator:<surname>` and Organization `id` values as `urn:cm4ai:org:<abbrev>`. These identifiers are not attested anywhere in the bundle. They are structurally valid uriorcurie but are fabricated identifiers rather than transcribed ones. The same applies to `urn:nih:grant:*` and `urn:uva:grant:frederick-thomas-fund` in `funders[*].grants[*].id`, and to all `urn:cm4ai:subset:*` and `urn:cm4ai:filecollection:*` identifiers in the full record.

`project_administration` and `funding_acquisition` are assigned to Ideker, and `investigation` to Krogan and Lundberg. All three are defined CREDiT enum values. The bundle supports Ideker as PI and corresponding author and supports Krogan/Lundberg laboratories as data generators, but does not use CREDiT vocabulary; the mapping is inferential. Note also that the Nature paper's Contributions section — which does describe roles — concerns the U2OS study, not this dataset.

The `name` field carries a parenthetical bundle of three distinct identifiers and a dollar amount: '(1OT2OD032742-01; core project OT2OD032742; award 3OT2OD032742-01S2 for fiscal year 2025, USD 5,289,382)'. This is source commentary and multiple identifiers embedded inside a name value. Per the evidence boundary, identifier and amount content does not belong inside a name string.

Three FundingMechanism objects are emitted. The Nature 2025 acknowledgements in the bundle list further funders of that U2OS study (Schmidt Futures, Cancer Cell Map Initiative U54 CA274502, Cytoscape 5U24HG012107, NDEx 5U24CA269436, Canada Foundation for Innovation, Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, Goran Gustafsson Foundation, NIH R01GM083960 and P41GM109824). Correctly excluded, since they fund the U2OS work rather than CM4AI. Recorded as a deliberate boundary decision, not a defect.

`start_date: 2022-09-01` and `end_date: 2026-08-31` are transcribed from the NIH RePORTER project period, not from any statement about when data were collected. The project award window is not the data collection window; the bundle gives no collection start or end date. The `source_caveats` discloses a conflict with the November 2026 figure but not the more basic substitution of award period for collection period.

Set true with details citing GO/Reactome alignment and LLM naming. In the bundle these are annotation and evaluation steps applied to computed cell maps, which this release explicitly does not contain. The validation described therefore does not apply to any instance in the released data.

All four PreprocessingStrategy objects describe the MuSIC embedding, co-embedding and community-detection pipeline. The bundle states plainly that 'Computed cell maps not included in this release'. These steps were therefore not applied to the data being described; they describe a downstream pipeline whose outputs are absent. Same concern applies to `labeling_strategies` (both objects annotate cell map assemblies) and `machine_annotation_tools`.

Conflates two unrelated claims: perturb-seq QC ('The resulting data are currently being QCed' in the preprint, i.e. in progress at preprint time) and FAIRSCAPE schema validation of pipeline inputs. Neither is a data cleaning strategy in the sense the slot describes (outlier removal, deduplication, error correction), and the first is stated in the bundle as pending rather than completed.

Contains the inline fragment 'The June 2026 release records De-identified Samples: Yes.' — source commentary about where a value was transcribed from, embedded in a content field rather than placed in `source_caveats`. Same pattern in `human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance` ('The release records Human Subjects: No and FDA Regulated: No').
Contains 'All files in the release are marked File Access: Public' — transcription commentary about the source record's UI labels rather than a statement about the data's confidentiality.

Both EthicalReview objects use `reviewing_organization` to name the contact's employing institution (The Hastings Center, Simon Fraser University). The bundle names Ravitsky and Belisle-Pipon as ethical review contacts for CM4AI; it does not state that either institution performed an ethical review of this dataset. No IRB, ethics committee or approval number is attested anywhere in the bundle — consistent with the record's own `involves_human_subjects: false`.

Ravitsky's ORCID is transcribed from the Dataverse author list where her affiliation is University of Montreal; the record assigns her to The Hastings Center in `reviewing_organization` (supported by the release's ethics contact email) and lists both institutions under `creators[13].affiliations`. Internally consistent but the two organizational attributions come from different parts of the bundle.

UCSD is asserted as the accountable organization. The bundle names a UCSD-affiliated governance contact (Jillian Parker, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) but does not state which organization is accountable for the data over time. The copyright statement names the Regents of the University of California, Stanford, and UCSF variously; the LibraData deposit sits at the University of Virginia. Single-organization accountability is inferred.

`unrestricted` is asserted. The dataset is CC BY-NC-SA licensed with a commercial-use prohibition, a Data Access Committee, and some components under embargo. `unrestricted` overstates openness relative to the bundle's own access terms.

Omitted. The digest offers `not_applicable`, which the bundle supports directly — the release records Human Subjects: No, de-identified samples, and non-clinical cell-line origin. A clearly supported enum value is unpopulated.

Set `true` with donor demographics of the two source cell lines. The slot describes subpopulations represented *within the dataset*; cell-line donor provenance is not a subpopulation structure in the data. The information is bundle-supported and correctly placed nowhere else in the schema, but the boolean asserts a property of the dataset that does not hold in the sense the slot intends.

Seven DataSubset objects are emitted with `is_data_split: false` and `is_subpopulation: false` on each. If both flags are false the objects assert they are neither splits nor subpopulations, which leaves their status as 'subsets' unexplained. The conditions themselves are well-supported by the bundle; the two false flags together are uninformative.

Omitted from the core record while present in the full record with seven entries. `subsets` is listed among the schema slots; if CoreDataset admits it, the seven condition arms are as bundle-supported in the core as in the full record and the asymmetry is unjustified. If CoreDataset does not admit it, no defect — but the digest supplied covers only Dataset.

Present-in-full, absent-in-core: `relationships` (cell map DAG structure), `file_collections` (six collections), `total_file_count` (10), `citation` (full recommended citation, relocated into `notes` prose in the core record). The `citation` relocation in particular moves structured content into free text; if CoreDataset declares `citation`, the field should hold it.

The core `notes` carries the full recommended citation as prose. Per the notes slot description, notes is for residual content only after every fitting slot is used; `citation` is a fitting slot and is populated in the full record.

`id` is the June 2026 release DOI, scoping the record to one quarterly release. Yet `name: CM4AI`, the `description`'s first three paragraphs, `purposes`, `addressing_gaps`, `tasks`, `funders`, `collection_mechanisms`, `preprocessing_strategies` and most of `notes` describe the CM4AI project as a whole across all releases. The referent oscillates between project and release.

Range is string; a prose sentence naming both cell lines with RRIDs and sources is supplied. The slot description asks for 'a resource from which this resource was derived'. Two resources are packed into one string. Shape is technically valid but the value is not a resource reference.

`https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/` is a repository base URL rather than an organization identifier. Range is uriorcurie so the shape validates; the bundle supports 'University of Virginia Dataverse' / LibraData as the publishing venue.

The value describes RO-Crate packaging, JSON-LD/Schema.org/EVI metadata, JSON-Schema data dictionaries and ARK identifiers. These are properties of the *metadata packaging*, not standards the dataset's own content follows. The slot description distinguishes content standards (DICOM, WFDB, BIDS, OMOP) from datasheet-schema statements; RO-Crate packaging sits closer to the latter. `conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]` is a defined enum value so the paired term is admissible.

`2026-07-15T00:00:00Z` is taken from the publication date of the three immunofluorescence image files within the June 2026 record. The bundle gives no dataset-level last-modified timestamp; a per-file publication date is substituted.

`2025-02-27T00:00:00Z` is the Dataverse 'Data Creation Date' and 'Deposit Date' for the record, both of which predate the June 2026 release by sixteen months and are carried over unchanged from the March 2025 deposit. It is transcribed accurately but does not describe when the June 2026 release was created.

`'May 2024'` is a free-text month-year among sibling entries using ISO dates ('2025-03-03', '2026-06-17'). Inconsistent value shape within one multivalued slot. The bundle supports 'May 2024 Data Release' as a label but gives no precise date for it.

Points to the June 2025 release DOI. That DOI resolves to the corrected dataset, not to an erratum notice. The bundle records the correction inside the June 2025 description text; there is no separate erratum document.

All three prior releases are typed `is_new_version_of`. That relationship correctly describes June 2026 relative to October 2025, but June 2026 is not directly a new version of both June 2025 and March 2025 — those are earlier links in the same chain. The digest offers `is_previous_version_of`, `replaces`, `continues` and `has_version`; a chain of successive versions is flattened.

DatasetRelationship required keys are `relationship_type` and `target_dataset`, and it accepts the top-level slot listing, so `name` and `description` are admissible. No defect; recorded for completeness.

Cites Nourreddine et al., the iPSC perturbation atlas preprint. That preprint is listed in the bundle's Related Publication field but its full text is not in the declared bundle; the claim that its findings 'were validated by phenotypic, protein-interaction and metabolic tracing assays' is transcribed from the March 2025 Dataverse abstract, which is in the bundle. Supported, but the abstract describes the atlas dataset's own validation rather than a third-party use of this release.

'38 participants registered' for the CodeFest is bundle-supported but describes a training event attendance figure, not a use of the dataset. The preceding clause about tutorials and software is the actual use claim.

States that proteome-wide SEC-MS and genome-scale CRISPRi 'broaden coverage beyond the targeted panel'. This is accurate for the KOLF2.1J CRISPRi atlas (11,739 genes) but the record's own `known_limitations` states the three modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets. Presenting broadened coverage as mitigation for selection bias overstates what the bundle supports.

The Nature 2025 U2OS study is listed as an external resource with a full paragraph of its findings and portal URLs. The record's `source_caveats` correctly states that no U2OS findings are attributed to this dataset. However `external_resources.external_resources` is a description field and the entry reads as a summary of a different study rather than a resource reference, edging toward importing out-of-scope content.

`archival: true` is asserted for MassIVE, NCBI SRA, Figshare and LibraData. The bundle supports the LibraData claim explicitly ('Long term preservation ... supported by committed institutional funds'). For MassIVE, SRA and Figshare the bundle records only that data are deposited there; archival guarantees are inferred.

findings.slot: collection_consents / collection_notifications / consent_revocations / informed_consent / participant_privacy / participant_compensation / at_risk_populations / data_protection_impacts / content_warnings
findings.issue: All omitted. Correct: `involves_human_subjects: false` and the cell-line origin make every consent, notification, revocation, privacy, compensation, at-risk and DPIA slot inapplicable, and the bundle attests no content warnings. Recorded as verified-correct omissions rather than defects.

Omitted from both records (the full record does not carry it either, contrary to what a full/core diff might suggest). The bundle supports at least one anomaly-adjacent fact: the March 2025 release covered 563 proteins in the IF images while June 2025 onward cover 464, a coverage reduction the record discloses only in `source_caveats`. Whether that is a DataAnomaly or a version difference is arguable; flagged as a candidate omission.
Omitted. Correct — the bundle describes no train/validation/test partitioning of these data.

Omitted from both records while `page` is populated. The bundle supplies the Dataverse Data Access API base (`https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/`) and the dataset landing URL. The API base is a template requiring a file id rather than a direct download URL, so omission is defensible; noted because a downloadable-file route is attested.
Omitted with a stated rationale in `source_caveats` (per-file sizes are rounded). Correct and well-disclosed.
Omitted. The bundle names no citation index, papers-with-code entry or use-tracking resource for this dataset. Correct omission.

All omitted. The bundle supplies no per-variable metadata, no inter-annotator agreement statistics, no imputation, and no discouraged-as-distinct-from-prohibited uses. `raw_sources` (RawData) overlaps `raw_data_sources` (RawDataSource), which is populated with ten entries; using one of the two overlapping slots is reasonable.

Present in the full record with one ThirdPartySharing object; absent from the core record. The MassIVE/SRA/Figshare distribution and the CFDE collaboration are equally bundle-supported for both records. Unexplained asymmetry.
Present in full (`is_direct: true` with cell-line sourcing detail); absent from core. Same asymmetry pattern.

`beta` is used. The bundle titles every release '(Beta)', so the value is supported. The slot description's examples are draft/published/deprecated; `beta` is not from a closed enum (range is string) so the shape validates.

`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` as a bare string. Bundle-supported verbatim from the Dataverse License/Data Use Agreement field. The canonical URL `https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/` is also in the bundle and would be a more resolvable value, but range is string and the label is what the source states.

The description's final paragraph enumerates the June 2026 release contents, but the preceding three paragraphs describe project scope, cell lines, the MuSIC pipeline and FAIRSCAPE packaging — content that duplicates `purposes`, `collection_mechanisms`, `preprocessing_strategies` and `conforms_to`. Per the notes/description ordering rule, structured slots come first and description holds what they cannot; substantial duplication here.

The dataset-level `source_caveats` correctly flags the U2OS boundary, the June 2026 date conflict, the project-end-date conflict, the project-wide-count scoping, the creator subsetting, and the 563-vs-464 protein-count change. Well-executed. One gap: it does not flag that `collection_timeframes` substitutes the NIH award period for a data collection period, nor that `preprocessing_strategies` and `labeling_strategies` describe a pipeline whose outputs are absent from this release.

summary: Both records are substantially grounded in the declared bundle and carry unusually candid dataset-level source_caveats — the U2OS/Nature boundary is correctly policed, the creator subsetting is disclosed, and the project-wide vs. per-release count scoping is flagged. No fabricated dataset facts were found. The material defects fall into five groups. (1) Shape: the core record's `distributions` block (ten objects with `path`/`md5`/`compression` keys) is not attested in the supplied schema digest and is the highest validation risk; a grant `name` value carries three identifiers and a dollar figure as embedded commentary. (2) Referent drift: `id` and `doi` scope both records to the June 2026 release, but description, purposes, tasks, funders and collection_mechanisms describe the CM4AI project across all releases, and `instances[0].counts` imports a project-wide image count into a per-release record. (3) Pipeline-vs-release mismatch: preprocessing_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools and acquisition_methods[2] all describe MuSIC cell-map construction, while the bundle states plainly that computed cell maps are not in this release — these describe steps not applied to the released data. (4) Full/core asymmetry without justification: relationships, file_collections, total_file_count, citation, subsets, third_party_sharing and direct_collection are present in full and absent from core; citation in particular is relocated into core `notes` prose. (5) Inference beyond evidence, mostly low-severity: collection_timeframes substitutes the NIH award window for a collection window; data_governance.accountable_organization picks one of three copyright-holding institutions; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level asserts `unrestricted` despite NC licensing, a Data Access Committee and embargoed components; archival flags are asserted for MassIVE/SRA/Figshare on deposit alone; ~30 minted urn: identifiers appear nowhere in the bundle. Two clearly-supported omissions: regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant should be `not_applicable`, and creators could carry all ~46 attested contributors rather than sixteen. Consent, privacy, at-risk-population and DPIA omissions are correct given involves_human_subjects: false.
